long_biography.plain_text:
Royal Jordanian's early expansion required more than aircraft and routes: it needed local pilots, engineers and technicians. Ali Ghandour answered that shortage by creating an aero club at Amman airport, teaching its first ground courses and developing the institution that became the Royal Jordanian Air Academy.

The training project sat inside a wider programme of aviation building. As Royal Jordanian's chairman and president, Ghandour helped establish cargo, executive-aircraft and aerobatic operations, while the academy supplied professional crews to carriers across the region. He later carried that experience to airline boards, aviation organisations and university trusteeship.
